To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a subpopulation (20%) of the mouse subthalamic nucleus contains neurons with profuse local axon collatterals, and that these neurons have the ability to generate intrinsic plateau potentials.
a subpopulation (20%) of STN neurons possesses a highly branched axon and dendrites, which allows them to generate plateau potentials and to synchronize with other STN neurons.
“a subpopulation of STH neurons with local axons and dendrites, can amplify hyperdirect cortical input and synchronize the STN population”.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new types of STN neurons with local axonal branching.
a new sub‐population of STN neuron, which could play an important role in the generation of pathological oscillations and the pathophysiology of Parkinson's disease.
the identification of new neuronal subtypes and the study of the mechanisms underlying the generation of their electrophysiological characteristics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a subpopulation, about 20% of STN neurons, born at E11.5‐E12.5, have the intrinsic properties to form an intra‐STN network that is able to synchronize the STN neuronal network.
the subthalamic neurons with local axons are a distinct subpopulation of neurons that are not only morphologically but also electrophysiologically different from the neurons without local axons.
STN neurons with local axonal collaterals form a new type of subpopulation that is distinct from the previously identified STN neuronal subpopulations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a subpopulation (20%) of the STN neurons, which are born at E11.5 and E12.5, have the ability to generate local glutamateric feedback excitation and that they are the most likely candidates to form a local network.

a subset of STN neurons, born at E11.5, has the ability to form local glutamateric network, and that these neurons have intrinsic electrophysiology properties similar to that of the classical STN neurons.

a subpopulation (20%) of STN neurons with a narrow time window of birth (E11–E12) and a specific morphology, have the ability to generate intrinsic plateaux, which could contribute to the synchronization of the STH neuronal network.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the neuronal population of the STN is more complex than previously thought, with the existence of a subpopulation of neurons that are highly collateralized, and that could play a key role in the amplification of cortical inputs.
the STN neuronal network is more complex than previously described and that the STN network is not a simple relay station for the basal ganglia.
the STN is not a homogeneous structure but rather a mosaic of neuronal populations with distinct intrinsic properties and connectivity.
